editions.label: 18 Nov
editions.title: Portugal property investment tops €1.9bn by Q3 — hotels and logistics drive a record year
editions.summary: Commercial real-estate investment reached roughly €1.9–2.1 billion in the first nine months of 2026, up between 3% and 11% depending on whose data you read (Savills, CBRE, Dils, Worx). Hotels led every table, drawing close to €590 million and rising more than 50% as the 2030 World Cup pipeline fills. Industrial and logistics surged around 68%, powered by an AI-driven data-centre wave. Foreign capital now supplies 72–75% of all volume, with the UK, France, Spain and the US writing the biggest cheques. The forecasters split on the finish: CBRE sees more than €3 billion for 2026, Worx a cooler €2.6–2.75 billion. Net: money is flowing freely, but it is chasing yield and operating assets — not trophy offices.
editions.hook: The capital keeps coming — and Portugal is on track for a record year.

items.headline: Quadrantis Capital buys Lisbon's Karl Lagerfeld Residences from Overseas
items.summary: Quadrantis took 100% of the company behind the project — ten exclusive homes in Lisbon, the fashion house's first branded-residence scheme in Portugal — via an SPV it is converting into a regulated SIC fund. Overseas stays on as developer; construction is slated for Q1 2027.
items.why: Branded residences wrapped in a fund vehicle are exactly the luxury-meets-institutional play pulling foreign capital into Portugal — a template for packaging trophy residential as something you can actually invest in.

items.headline: Casas do Barlavento absorbs PPI to deepen its western Algarve grip
items.summary: The Lagos-based agency bought the office and client book of PPI – Real Estate, extending into Vila do Bispo, Salema and Sagres and retaining the whole PPI team. Terms were not disclosed; the deal formally closed on 1 October.
items.why: Brokerage consolidation in the Algarve is a maturing-market signal — the agencies with the deepest local networks are buying distribution ahead of the next cycle.

items.headline: Arrow Global grabs the Tróia Design Hotel as Évora lands a data centre
items.summary: Arrow Global bought the Tróia Design Hotel and Spain's NxN entered Portugal with a ~1 MW data centre in Évora, part of a Q3 that Dils puts at €630 million (+33% on the prior quarter). Retail stayed busy too, including the sale of Forum Algarve.
items.why: The deal mix — hospitality, data centres, dominant retail — shows where operating income is being underwritten. Land and development feed these, but capital is paying up for assets that already throw off cash.

items.headline: AI is pulling a new wave of data-centre capital toward Portugal
items.summary: Cheap renewable power, Atlantic cable landings and Europe's tightening grid are steering AI-era data-centre money to Portugal — with Microsoft's multi-billion Sines commitment the anchor and new entrants like NxN now building. JLL flags the country as a European standout for campus development.
items.why: Data centres are the fastest-growing slice of Portuguese real estate and a structurally new land use. Owners of grid-connected, power-rich sites hold an increasingly scarce asset.

items.headline: The new rent law quietly tilts back toward landlords
items.summary: The government's arrendamento reform — approved in general terms and now in committee — would let landlords start eviction after two months of arrears (down from three), lift advance rent to three months, scrap the deposit cap and end rent control on new contracts. Existing contracts stay under current rules until the final text passes.
items.why: If it survives committee intact, the reform materially lowers the risk premium on Portuguese rental income — the single biggest deterrent for institutional build-to-rent capital.

items.headline: EIB puts €300m behind affordable rental
items.summary: Lisbon and the European Investment Bank signed a €300 million IFRRU 2030 line for moderate-rent housing, split into Build-to-Rent and Renovate-to-Rent strands and channelled mainly to private developers through financial intermediaries. It follows €1.34bn and €1.5bn earlier EIB housing lines.
items.why: Public-backed, below-market financing de-risks affordable BtR — a direct subsidy to the supply side that developers with the right pipeline can tap.

items.headline: House prices still climbing 13% — even as sales fall
items.summary: Home prices rose 13.1% year-on-year in Q3 to an average €3,416/m² even as transactions dropped 12.5% to about 36,000, per JLL. Porto (+14.7% to €4,382/m²) outran Lisbon (+7.4% to €5,963/m²).
items.why: Prices decoupling from volumes is a supply-shortage signal, not a demand surge — scarcity, not froth, is doing the work, which favours anyone who can actually deliver new stock.

items.headline: The pros are pointing at middle-class rental
items.summary: Mid-market rental housing is "one of the best investment opportunities" in Portugal right now, industry voices argue: the squeezed middle is under-served, demand per listing is running at record multiples, and yields beat prime.
items.why: The thesis lines up with the policy tailwinds — EIB money, a landlord-friendlier law. The gap between what the middle class can pay and what the market supplies is where risk-adjusted returns sit.

readForFund.text: Capital is paying up for hotels, logistics and data centres while offices and "living" soften. Underwrite operating income.
A landlord-friendlier rent law plus €300m of EIB BtR money lowers the risk premium on Portuguese rental — the case for middle-market residential is strengthening.
Grid-connected, renewable-fed land is becoming the scarce input behind the fastest-growing asset class. Sites with capacity are worth more than they look.
Prices up 13% on falling sales means supply is the binding constraint — the edge is in delivery, not discovery.

editions.label: 17 Nov
editions.title: Corum's biggest-ever Portugal deal caps a €1.9bn quarter of surging capital
editions.summary: Portuguese real estate investment accelerated again in the third quarter, with activity climbing 33% over the prior quarter and the market pushing past €1.9 billion. The clearest signal came from Corum, whose purchase of the Green Park office complex is now its largest-ever deal in Portugal — a foreign fund doubling down, not retreating. Beneath the headline numbers, capital is rotating into flexible offices, retail and alternatives as prime yields compress. At the opportunistic end, a real-estate group paid €33 million for Boavista's Estádio do Bessa at auction. Prices, meanwhile, keep grinding higher — up 1.9% in November alone. Net: liquidity is abundant and turning more selective — the edge now is sourcing, not access.
editions.hook: The capital isn't cooling — Portugal's funds are just going bigger.

items.headline: Corum's Green Park buy is its biggest-ever Portugal deal
items.summary: French open-ended fund manager Corum has acquired the Green Park office complex in a transaction it describes as its largest operation in Portugal to date, deepening an already substantial Lisbon office portfolio.
items.why: A core European fund scaling up — not trimming — signals institutional money still reads Lisbon offices as a buy, even after yields have compressed.

items.headline: A property group buys Estádio do Bessa for €33m
items.summary: A real-estate group linked to the Maurício family signed the deed to acquire Boavista FC's Estádio do Bessa and its surrounding sports complex for €33 million, closing out a contested auction of the Euro 2004 venue.
items.why: Distressed sports and institutional assets are turning into live development plays — Portugal's best basis is often found in forced sales, not open-market listings.

items.headline: A landmark author's building in central Lisbon starts a new era
items.summary: A heritage 'imóvel de autor' in the heart of Lisbon is being repositioned into a renewed residential project — the latest in a run of central-Lisbon conversions trading on the scarcity of prime, characterful stock.
items.why: Conversion of signature central assets is where value is being created as new-build land runs dry — the margin sits in planning and restoration, not in the dirt.

items.headline: A Douro house wins Portuguese architecture a Silver in Madrid
items.summary: A contemporary house in the Douro by a Portuguese studio took a Silver distinction at an international awards in Madrid, extending a strong year for the country's residential architecture abroad.
items.why: Design pedigree is a pricing lever in Portugal's prime and resort segments — award-winning architecture is how developers increasingly justify premiums.

items.headline: Concreta 2026 maps where building and design go next
items.summary: The Concreta fair in Porto gathered the construction and architecture trade around new materials, methods and the sector's shifting priorities for the year ahead.
items.why: Construction-cost and method innovation is the real lever on development margin — what shows at Concreta previews where build budgets are heading.

items.headline: Could European housing models fix Portugal's crisis?
items.summary: A new analysis weighs whether policy models from elsewhere in Europe — from rent regulation to public-private supply schemes — could be adapted to ease Portugal's housing shortage, as the Government's reform package advances.
items.why: Housing policy is now the single biggest swing factor for residential returns — whichever European template Portugal borrows will reshape rent controls, supply incentives and development risk.

items.headline: Investment tops €1.9bn, up 33% in a single quarter
items.summary: Portuguese real estate investment accelerated sharply in Q3, climbing about 33% over the prior quarter and pushing the market past €1.9 billion as transaction activity kept rising.
items.why: Volume and velocity rising together is the clearest sign yet that the recovery is broad-based — not a handful of trophy trades.

items.headline: Flexible offices gain ground as occupiers chase agility
items.summary: Demand for tailored and flexible office space is strengthening across Portugal, with companies prioritising agility and shorter commitments — a shift reshaping how landlords underwrite office stock.
items.why: The flex pivot changes office cash flows and exit assumptions — owners who can offer flexibility capture the demand rigid long-lease product is losing.

items.headline: House prices climb another 1.9% in November
items.summary: Sale prices rose 1.9% month-on-month in November, per idealista's index, extending a long record run and keeping affordability firmly in the political spotlight.
items.why: Relentless price growth sustains the policy risk around housing — and widens the gap any new supply has to close before values ease.

readForFund.lead: Underwrite the surge, not the dip.
readForFund.text: With investment up a third in a quarter and prices still rising, waiting for a correction is the riskier bet — discipline has to come from basis and sourcing, not timing.
Corum going bigger shows core European capital is still buying Lisbon offices — co-investing alongside that flow beats competing head-on with it.

readForFund.lead: The margin is in the mess.
readForFund.text: This week's best entries — a €33m stadium at auction, a heritage Lisbon conversion — came from distress and complexity, not clean listings.
Rental reform and the housing-policy debate are the real swing factor for residential returns — underwrite the regime you'll actually operate under, not today's.

editions.label: 16 Nov
editions.title: Portugal commercial property nears €2bn in 9 months — hotels +51%, CBRE sees a €3bn year
editions.summary: Portugal drew €1.9bn of commercial real estate in the first nine months of 2026 — and CBRE thinks the full year clears €3bn. Hotels are doing the heavy lifting: €588m, 31% of the total, up 51% year-on-year. Logistics is the other engine, up 68% to €248m. Retail and offices softened, and the living sector fell hard as student-housing deals dried up. Foreign capital now drives 72% of volume, mostly Spain, the UK, France and the US. Deal count rose 36% even as average ticket sizes shrank — more shots on goal, smaller cheques. Net: the money is here and getting more selective; underwriting, not sourcing, is where this cycle is won.
editions.hook: Capital isn't cooling — Portugal's year is shaping up as one of its biggest ever.

items.headline: Confrasilvas signs the €33M deed for Boavista's Bessa stadium
items.summary: The Lisbon group Confrasilvas — through Frozenpark, Boavista's largest creditor — completed the purchase of the roughly 78,000 m² Estádio do Bessa and its complex for €33 million, with the deed signed this week via auctioneer Leilosoc. No redevelopment plan has been disclosed.
items.why: A Euro 2004 stadium on 78,000 m² of Porto land, taken out of insolvency by its own creditor, is a rare large urban site whose next use will set a local benchmark.

items.headline: €180M share deal changes hands at Arrábida and Gaia shopping centres
items.summary: Savills flags a €180 million share transaction for stakes in Arrábida Shopping and Gaia Shopping among the quarter's larger trades — even as overall shopping-centre volume fell sharply year-on-year, from €547m to €245m.
items.why: Prime, dominant malls still clear — buyers are paying up for the few assets with pricing power while secondary retail reprices.

items.headline: InHabitus bets on factory-built homes, targets 1,080 units by 2028
items.summary: The Porto developer is building condominium homes off-site — around 80% factory-made — with prices from €139,000. Its €15M, 79-home Alfena scheme is sold out awaiting a licence, a €24M, 136-home Setúbal project is 80% reserved, and the pipeline spans Viseu, Campanhã, Benavente and Paredes.
items.why: Industrialised construction plus the 6% VAT band is one of the few credible routes to building sub-€150k homes at scale and a margin — a model to watch for anyone underwriting affordable supply.

items.headline: Marta Costa takes the helm at state-backed Fomento Fundos
items.summary: Marta Costa has been named director-general of Fomento Fundos, the Banco Português de Fomento group's real-estate fund manager behind the Fundo Especial de Apoio às Empresas and Fundo Revive Natureza. She arrives from HR leadership at Vanguard and earlier government investment-promotion roles.
items.why: The state's property-fund vehicle steers public capital into tourism and industrial assets — who runs it shapes where co-investment and JV openings appear.

items.headline: Braga's Casa S wins at the 2026 Architecture MasterPrize
items.summary: Casa S, a single-family house on a wooded Braga hillside by L2C Arquitetura (Luís Cunha), took the Residential — Single Family winner's prize at the Architecture MasterPrize 2026, with the ceremony set for the Guggenheim in Bilbao.
items.why: Portugal's design reputation keeps compounding at the top end — a selling point that underpins premium pricing on well-designed residential stock.

items.headline: 2027 Budget keeps the housing playbook: under-35 IMT break, 6% build VAT
items.summary: The OE2027 proposal retains the IMT and stamp-duty exemption for first-time buyers aged 35 and under — ceiling rising to €338,141 — keeps the 6% VAT rate for moderately priced construction, and adds IRS relief on rents up to €2,300/month (a €209M cost). Lisbon forecasts IMI revenue down 5.6% and IMT down 2.3%.
items.why: The under-35 break has already moved ~120,000 buyers at ~€200k average; its continuation plus the 6% build VAT keeps demand and supply incentives pointed the same way into 2027.

items.headline: Commercial investment hits €1.9bn in nine months; CBRE sees a €3bn year
items.summary: Savills puts nine-month commercial volume at €1.9bn (+3% y/y), led by hotels (€588m, +51%) and logistics (+68%), while CBRE's read is ~€2bn and it forecasts the full year above €3bn. Prime yields held near 5.6% against ~4% on 10-year bonds; 75 deals closed (+36%) at a smaller €24.9m average ticket.
items.why: A ~1.6-point spread over sovereigns, with hotels and sheds compounding, keeps Portugal priced for income — the case for selective entry over broad beta.

items.headline: Asking prices hit a record €3,249/m², up 7.5% in October
items.summary: idealista's October index shows national asking prices at an all-time high of €3,249/m², +7.5% y/y, with Lisbon at €6,248/m² and Porto at €4,339/m². INE's Q2 transaction data separately marks a €2,445/m² record even as sales fell 9%.
items.why: Prices keep setting records while volumes slide — a thinner, pricier market that rewards buying right over buying fast.

readForFund.text: With 75 deals but shrinking tickets, the 2026 edge is pricing discipline on a crowded field, not deal access.
Hotels (+51%) and logistics (+68%) are where capital compounds; retail and student housing are repricing — position accordingly.
The under-35 IMT break and 6% build VAT keep affordable demand and construction economics aligned into 2027.
New price highs on falling volumes mean the next leg is about asset selection and basis, not riding the market.

editions.label: 15 Nov
editions.title: €1.9bn floods Portuguese property — hotels +51%, logistics +68%, foreign buyers now 72%
editions.summary: Commercial real-estate investment hit €1.9bn in the first nine months of 2026, with Q3 the strongest quarter of the year. Hotels led at €588m (+51%) and industrial & logistics jumped 68%, while offices and student housing cooled. Foreign capital took 72% of the total, up from 62% a year earlier. Yet the same week, tens of thousands marched in more than 30 towns against an affordability crisis — house prices up nearly 20% in a year, rents up 68% since 2020. Parliament has just approved faster evictions and looser rental contracts, which protesters want reversed. Net: conviction and political risk are rising together — back Portugal's demand story, but underwrite the rental-rule fight.
editions.hook: Money is pouring in — just as the housing backlash boils over.

items.headline: FrozenPark pays €33m for Boavista's Bessa stadium out of insolvency
items.summary: An investor group took the bulk of Boavista FC's real estate — the Estádio do Bessa, its ~78,000 m² sports complex and a 21,145 m² plot with PDM development potential — via the club's insolvency, now holding roughly 70% of its debts.
items.why: Value in a supply-short city is unlocked through distressed routes and re-zonable land, not open-market bidding — a template for patient capital.

items.headline: Corum buys the 15,000 m² Green Park office in Lisbon from Incus Capital
items.summary: French manager Corum Investments acquired the office-and-retail Green Park on Avenida dos Combatentes — let to CTT, Pierre Fabre and Maló Clinic — lifting its Portuguese AUM above €250m. Price undisclosed.
items.why: A core open-ended fund — the CORUM model Verde tracks closely — doubling down on well-let Lisbon offices signals income buyers still back prime Portuguese yield over bonds.

items.headline: Prowinko sells a Chiado retail building to a private investor
items.summary: Dutch investor Prowinko offloaded a prime high-street retail asset in Lisbon's Chiado to a private buyer, one of several central-Lisbon retail trades this autumn.
items.why: Prime high-street retail — the segment hit hardest post-2020 — is trading again to private capital, a sign liquidity is returning at the top end.

items.headline: Quadrantis Capital buys the Karl Lagerfeld Residences from Overseas
items.summary: Quadrantis Capital acquired the branded Karl Lagerfeld Residences scheme from developer Overseas, keeping a marquee luxury-residences project in play.
items.why: Branded residences remain one of the few liquid luxury niches, pulling international capital even as mainstream prices stir political heat.

items.headline: Grupo Mais pivots to build-to-rent with 700+ homes in the pipeline
items.summary: The Fátima-based developer is shifting from build-to-sell to build-to-rent, with more than 700 homes — including student and key-worker housing — across central and southern Portugal, sited near universities, hospitals and employment hubs.
items.why: A domestic developer institutionalising rental supply confirms BTR/living is maturing beyond Lisbon and Porto — the demand thesis a fund underwrites.

items.headline: State launches a €16m revamp of Burnay Palace in western Lisbon
items.summary: The government opened a public design competition to restore the €15.76m Burnay Palace complex — palace, annexes and garden — into a cultural hub and a new headquarters for Museus e Monumentos, anchoring the Junqueira–Belém–Ajuda axis.
items.why: Public heritage regeneration raises the floor on surrounding land and residential values along one of Lisbon's prime riverside corridors.

items.headline: Unisana's Almada hospital secures €40m to expand
items.summary: Private operator Unisana lined up a €40m investment to enlarge its hospital on the south bank of the Tagus in Almada.
items.why: Healthcare real estate is drawing institutional money as a defensive, demographically-driven class — a diversifier for portfolios tilted to living and hospitality.

items.headline: Lisbon Triennale puts 16 studios to work rethinking the home
items.summary: The Lisbon Architecture Triennale gathers 16 ateliers in a show reimagining contemporary housing — a direct creative response to Portugal's affordability squeeze.
items.why: How the country's best studios answer the housing question shapes the product — and the planning narratives — developers will build next.

items.headline: Parliament speeds up evictions and loosens rental contracts — streets erupt
items.summary: After parliament approved more contract flexibility and faster eviction procedures, tens of thousands marched across 30+ towns on Saturday under the Casa Para Viver platform, demanding rent caps, stronger eviction protection and tighter short-let and vacancy rules. Portugal led the EU on rising price-to-income from 2015–25 (+61%), with rents up 68% since 2020.
items.why: The rules that govern letting are in open political contest — faster possession helps landlord underwriting now, but reversal risk, rent caps and an AL clampdown are live and must be priced into exits.

items.headline: Q3 reheats: €659m in a quarter, hotels and logistics carry the market
items.summary: Commercial investment reached €1.9bn in Jan–Sep (Savills, +3%; CBRE and Dils peg it nearer €2bn), with Q3's €659m up 38% on Q2. Hotels led at €588m (+51%) and industrial & logistics rose 68%, while offices (−17%) and living (−58%, student housing down to €75m) cooled. International buyers took 72%; CBRE sees full-year above €3bn.
items.why: Capital is concentrating in hospitality and logistics while offices and student housing correct — the sector rotation to underwrite into 2027.

readForFund.text: Hotels (+51%) and logistics (+68%) are where capital concentrates; offices and student housing are cooling — tilt pipeline and pricing to the segments still bid.
Faster evictions help landlord maths today, but reversal risk, rent caps and a short-let clampdown are in open contest — stress-test exits against a tighter regime.

readForFund.lead: Distress and rezoning are the alpha.
readForFund.text: The €33m Bessa buyout shows value is unlocked through insolvency and PDM development upside, not open-market bidding in a supply-short market.
A Fátima developer moving 700 homes to build-to-rent confirms the demand thesis is spreading nationwide — exactly the structural tailwind a fund backs.

editions.label: 14 Nov
editions.title: Portugal CRE investment hits €1.9bn, hotels in front; Corum lands its biggest Lisbon deal
editions.summary: Commercial real estate investment in Portugal reached €1.9 billion in the first nine months of 2026, up 3% on last year, on a €659m third quarter that jumped 38% on Q2. Hotels led every sector at €588m — nearly a third of all volume — as capital rotated out of shopping centres. International investors took 72% of the money, up from 62% a year ago, led by Spain, the UK, France and the US. Deal count rose 36% to 75 transactions, and CBRE now expects the full year to clear €3 billion. The same day, Corum closed its largest-ever Portuguese deal, buying Lisbon's Green Park office block and pushing its local book past €250m. Net: the money is still coming — and it is spreading across more sectors and more buyers.
editions.hook: €1.9bn in, hotels in front: Portugal's market is broadening, not cooling.

items.headline: Corum lands Green Park, its biggest Portuguese deal yet
items.summary: Corum Investments bought the Green Park office building on Lisbon's Avenida dos Combatentes from Incus Capital — roughly 15,000 m² of offices and retail let to CTT, Pierre Fabre and Malo Clinic. The price was undisclosed, but it is Corum's largest Portuguese acquisition and lifts its local book above €250m across 21 assets.
items.why: A €10bn open-ended manager doubling down on Lisbon offices — the defensive, income-first CORUM playbook that income funds (Verde 2050 included) study closely.

items.headline: Royal Ventures breaks into ground-up with a €15M Porto scheme
items.summary: The Porto developer is launching Royal Custóias in Matosinhos — its first ground-up build — with 51 T0–T2 apartments across about 4,000 m², designed by Pedro Pereira of Linhas & Traços. Pre-reservations open within weeks; construction starts in Q1 2027 and completes by end-2029.
items.why: A serial refurbisher moving to new-build middle-class housing signals where Porto margins now sit — and how long the build-to-sell cycle really runs.

items.headline: A Braga house takes a world architecture prize
items.summary: Casa S, a single-family home on a wooded Braga slope by Luís Cunha's studio L2C Arquitetura, won the Residential (Single Family) category at the Architecture MasterPrize 2026, judged against entries from 95 countries. The ceremony lands this November at the Guggenheim in Bilbao.
items.why: Portuguese residential design keeps winning global billing alongside Foster and Zaha Hadid — brand equity that sells homes and lifts land values around signature work.

items.headline: Commercial investment hits €1.9bn — and hotels are running the market
items.summary: Savills' Q3 report puts nine-month commercial volume at €1.9bn, +3% year-on-year, with hotels at €588m (31% of the total, +51%) as retail slipped 18%. Logistics (+68%) and data centres also gained; offices and living fell. CBRE sees the full year topping €3bn.
items.why: Capital is rotating — out of shopping centres, into hospitality, sheds and data — so the sector mix that worked in 2023 is not the one being rewarded now.

items.headline: House prices renew their record, up 7.5% in October
items.summary: Asking prices rose 7.5% year-on-year to a fresh all-time high, while separate Casafari data has used-flat values up about 10% in Q3 — T1s now average €281k and T4s €714k. Momentum is easing from the double-digit peaks, but it has not turned.
items.why: Still-rising prices against softening rents keep compressing gross yields — the squeeze that pushes income investors toward development and value-add over standing stock.

items.headline: Rents cool month-on-month, even as the annual line holds
items.summary: Median asking rents eased to €17.2/m² in October, +1% year-on-year but −6% on September; Lisbon stays dearest at €23.8/m², Porto at €18.3/m². Aveiro (+14%) and Évora (+8%) led the annual gains while Porto and Faro fell.
items.why: Rent growth is plateauing just as prices push on — a widening gap that makes underwriting new rental product harder and regional plays more interesting.

readForFund.text: Hotels, logistics and data centres are pulling capital that once defaulted to retail and offices — mix matters more than momentum now.

readForFund.lead: Foreign money is setting the price.
readForFund.text: At 72% of volume, international buyers are the marginal bidder — local sourcing and relationships are the edge.

readForFund.lead: Yields are tightening from both ends.
readForFund.text: Record prices plus cooling rents mean standing income looks thin — development and value-add carry the return.
Corum's €250m+ build and Royal's first ground-up say the same thing: conviction is in deploying, not waiting.

editions.label: 13 Nov
editions.title: Corum's biggest Portugal deal yet: Green Park lifts its Lisbon book past €250M
editions.summary: Corum has acquired Lisbon's Green Park office complex — its largest single operation in Portugal to date. The deal pushes the French manager's Portuguese book above €250 million, a conviction bet on prime offices even as space tightens. It lands the same week data showed commercial investment jumped 33% quarter-on-quarter to €630M, with foreign capital supplying three-quarters of the flow. Logistics is the other story: a 380,000 m² park is rising in Benavente, and Panattoni's Santarém hub just filled its last unit. Net: capital is concentrating in income-producing offices and logistics — and paying up for the best assets.
editions.hook: Corum just made its largest-ever bet on Lisbon offices.

items.headline: Corum buys Green Park, its biggest Portuguese deal
items.summary: Corum Investments has added the Green Park office complex in Lisbon to its funds, lifting its Portuguese portfolio above €250 million and making this its largest acquisition in the country.
items.why: A CORUM-style open-ended fund scaling up in prime Lisbon offices is the exact playbook Verde's model watches — it signals where income-focused capital still sees value.

items.headline: Forum Algarve sale makes retail the quarter's top sector
items.summary: Alfana Investment Management's purchase of the Forum Algarve shopping centre helped retail lead Q3 with roughly €195M — about 31% of all commercial investment in the quarter.
items.why: Dominant, grocery-anchored retail is being re-rated as a yield play — a reminder that "out of favour" sectors can reprice fast once income looks durable.

items.headline: A 380,000 m² logistics park rises in Benavente
items.summary: Benavente Prime Hub — a Davidson Kempner, ECS Capital and Magna joint venture — will deliver up to 380,000 m² across seven phases on a 630,000 m² site, all targeting BREEAM Excellent, with the first phase underway and full build-out by 2030.
items.why: Institutional money is still forward-committing to best-in-class sheds on the Lisbon logistics corridor — the clearest signal that occupier demand is outrunning modern supply.

items.headline: Panattoni Park Santarém hits 100% occupancy
items.summary: Panattoni's Santarém logistics park has filled its last available unit, reaching full occupancy as tenants compete for well-located space north of Lisbon.
items.why: Full occupancy at a new-build park underwrites the rents developers are pricing into the next wave of logistics schemes.

items.headline: An author-designed building in central Lisbon is reborn
items.summary: A landmark residential building in the heart of Lisbon is being rehabilitated into a new scheme, the latest in a steady pipeline of conversions reshaping the city's historic core.
items.why: Prime central rehab remains the default route to new homes in Lisbon, where land is scarce and heritage rules constrain ground-up delivery.

items.headline: A Douro house wins Portuguese architecture a Silver in Madrid
items.summary: A single-family house in the Douro has taken a Silver distinction at an international awards in Madrid, the latest in a strong run of recognition for Portuguese studios abroad.
items.why: Design pedigree is a marketing asset for developers — award-winning architecture helps sell schemes and sharpens Portugal's premium brand abroad.

items.headline: Loulé goes hunting for land and homes for public housing
items.summary: The Loulé council has opened a search to buy land and existing homes to expand its public and affordable housing stock, adding the municipality to the list of local buyers competing in the market.
items.why: Municipalities turning active buyers add a new source of demand — and a potential partner or exit — for developers and landowners in high-pressure markets like the Algarve.

items.headline: Commercial investment jumps 33% in Q3 to €630M
items.summary: Portuguese commercial real estate drew €630M in Q3 — up 33% on the prior quarter and €2bn year-to-date (+7% YoY) — with foreign capital at about 75% of volume and core strategies taking over 80%. Offices logged their best quarter of the year at €112M; logistics added €98M and hotels about €78M.
items.why: Momentum plus a heavy foreign, core-focused bid means pricing power sits with sellers of stabilised income — and competition for prime assets is only intensifying.

readForFund.text: The best Lisbon offices are trading on portfolio scale and covenant strength — the edge is moving decisively on income you can model, not hunting for price.
Benavente and Santarém show absorption running ahead of completions; forward-funding well-located sheds still clears.
With overseas money near 75% of Q3 volume, domestic players compete on speed and local knowledge, not cost of capital.
Forum Algarve led the quarter — dominant, grocery-anchored retail is being re-rated as a yield play.

editions.label: 12 Nov
editions.title: Portugal's property boom: ~€2bn invested by September, Q3 jumps 33% as foreign capital takes 75%
editions.summary: Commercial real estate in Portugal drew roughly €2bn of investment in the first nine months of 2026 — and the pace is accelerating, not fading. Q3 alone brought about €630m, up 33% on the prior quarter, with foreign investors taking 75% of it. Hotels (€590m) and logistics (€384m) have already beaten their full-year 2025 totals. Offices are the laggard, down around 40% year-to-date as money hunts yield elsewhere. Consultancies now peg the full year between €2.6bn and north of €3bn. Net: liquidity is back, and it's chasing beds and boxes over desks.
editions.hook: Capital isn't blinking: Portugal has pulled in ~€2bn before the year is even out.

items.headline: Quadrantis Capital buys the Karl Lagerfeld Residences in Lisbon
items.summary: Quadrantis Capital has acquired 100% of the company that owns the branded Karl Lagerfeld Residences Lisboa, buying the trophy residential scheme out of Overseas' hands.
items.why: Branded residences remain the one residential niche where Lisbon still prices like a global gateway — confirmation the luxury bid hasn't cooled even as mass-market volumes slip.

items.headline: Prowinko sells a Chiado retail building to a private investor
items.summary: Dutch investor Prowinko has offloaded a retail asset in Lisbon's Chiado — the city's prime high-street pitch — to a private buyer, a rare trade in one of Portugal's tightest retail markets.
items.why: Prime high-street assets rarely change hands; when they do, private capital — not institutions — is increasingly setting the clearing price in Lisbon's core.

items.headline: Grupo Mais places a big build-to-rent bet: 700 units
items.summary: Grupo Mais is committing to a major build-to-rent programme totalling around 700 homes, one of the larger institutional BTR moves yet seen in the Portuguese market.
items.why: BTR at scale is the structural bet on Portugal's rental shortage — and a signal that developers are finally underwriting rent rolls, not just exit sales.

items.headline: State puts €16M into restoring Lisbon's Burnay Palace
items.summary: The Portuguese government is investing roughly €16M to restore the historic Palácio Burnay in Lisbon, one of the capital's landmark heritage buildings.
items.why: Public heritage spend anchors value in Lisbon's historic core and often precedes a wave of private adaptive-reuse nearby — worth watching for spillover.

items.headline: A Saldanha office block is bought to become flats
items.summary: A fund managed by BPI Gestão de Ativos has sold Almirante Barroso 32 in Saldanha — a 4,500 sqm, seven-storey office — to a buyer planning to convert it into upper-middle and premium homes. Cushman & Wakefield advised, and notes about 20% of 2025 office investment went into assets bought for a change of use.
items.why: The office-to-resi arbitrage is now a strategy, not an exception. In central Lisbon, the discount on tired offices is the cheapest way into the housing bid.

items.headline: Savills names Alejandro Campoy CEO for Iberia
items.summary: Savills has promoted Alejandro Campoy, currently managing director, to CEO of Savills Iberia (Spain and Portugal) from early 2027. Jaime Pascual-Sanchiz steps up to run Continental Europe and becomes executive chairman of the Iberian business.
items.why: Another global agency is running Portugal and Spain as one desk. Expect cross-border capital to keep treating Iberia as a single investable market.

items.headline: The 2026 housing tax package rewards patient rental capital
items.summary: Decree-Law 97/2026 bundles Portugal's housing fiscal incentives, headlined by a capital-gains exemption when sale proceeds are reinvested into accessible or moderate-rent housing, alongside IMT, IRS and IVA measures aimed at putting stock on the long-term rental market.
items.why: The tax code is now tilting toward long-hold rental over quick resale — a real tailwind for funds underwriting accessible-rent strategies. Confirm specifics in the Diário da República before relying on them.

items.headline: Portugal leads the EU for house prices outrunning incomes
items.summary: Portugal is the EU country where house prices have climbed most relative to household incomes. Asking prices rose about 10% year-on-year in Q3 (used stock, per Casafari/DECO), with the price-to-income gap now the widest in the bloc — a growing affordability and political pressure point.
items.why: The wider the affordability gap, the heavier the policy risk — rent controls, transfer taxes and supply mandates all get more likely. Price that into long holds.

items.headline: Rents keep rising, but the momentum is finally cooling
items.summary: New-contract rents are still up year-on-year — around 4.5% on DECO's Q3 read — but October data shows the pace easing after a long run of acceleration, with month-on-month moves flattening.
items.why: Cooling rent growth alongside still-rising prices compresses yields. The easy rental re-rating is behind us; returns now hinge on buying well.

readForFund.text: With 75% of Q3 capital foreign and everyone chasing the same prime beds and sheds, edge is pricing risk faster than the crowd — not sourcing the asset.
Hotels (€590m) and logistics (€384m) have already topped all of 2025; offices are down ~40%. Tilt toward structural demand.
About a fifth of 2025 office volume was bought to convert. In Lisbon, the office discount is the residential entry point.
The 2026 fiscal package rewards reinvestment into accessible-rent housing — aligning long-hold rental strategies with tax relief.

editions.label: 11 Nov
editions.title: Portugal property investment hits €2bn in 9 months; Q3 jumps 33% to €630M
editions.summary: Portugal's commercial property market has posted €2bn of investment in nine months, up 7% on last year. The third quarter alone drew €630M — a 33% jump on the previous three. Foreign capital was 75% of the quarter, with core and core-plus strategies more than 80% of activity. Retail led the year at €611M, but logistics has already beaten its full-year 2025 total and offices just had their best quarter of 2026. Prime yields are tightening — high-street retail compressed to 4.25% after deals in Chiado. Net: this is a market being bid up by patient institutional money, not speculative froth.
editions.hook: Capital isn't cooling — Portugal pulled €2bn of property deals by September.

items.headline: Saqax buys Logispark Montijo from CBRE IM
items.summary: Dutch investor Saqax picked up the Logispark Montijo logistics scheme from CBRE Investment Management — one of the quarter's signature trades in a sector where demand jumped 60% year on year.
items.why: Prime logistics yields have compressed to 5.75% in both Lisbon and Porto — institutional buyers are paying up for the asset class with the cleanest income story.

items.headline: Arrow Global acquires the Tróia Design Hotel
items.summary: The Setúbal-peninsula resort hotel changed hands to Arrow Global, part of a hotel haul that has already pushed 2026 hotel investment to €590M — above both the 2024 and 2025 full-year totals.
items.why: Hospitality is now roughly 27% of all commercial capital deployed — credit-and-asset platforms are moving into operating hotels, not just distressed debt.

items.headline: Alfana makes its Portugal debut with Forum Algarve
items.summary: Alfana Investment Management entered Portugal by buying the Forum Algarve shopping centre, folding it into its Rivoli Retail platform — retail was the year's biggest segment at €611M despite sitting 8% below 2025.
items.why: A first-time entrant paying for a dominant regional mall signals that institutional appetite for Portuguese retail has turned the corner.

items.headline: Hotel pipeline swells by 3,253 rooms
items.summary: Portugal added 3,253 hotel rooms in the first nine months of 2026, with roughly 1,600 more due by year-end — openings include the Kimpton Quinta da Marinha in Cascais and Wilde Clérigos in Porto.
items.why: New supply is concentrating in the upper tier — Algarve ADR and RevPAR rose 3%, while Lisbon RevPAR slipped 5% as rooms come online faster than demand.

items.headline: Retail-park wave: seven schemes, 77,000 m²
items.summary: Seven retail parks totalling 77,000 m² are under construction across the country, with the 18,000 m² Beja Jardim Retail Park already open — the format quietly carrying Portugal's retail development pipeline.
items.why: Retail parks offer cheaper build costs and resilient convenience footfall — the lower-risk way to add retail GLA while shopping-centre yields sit at 6.25%.

items.headline: €2bn in nine months, three-quarters foreign
items.summary: Dils' Q3 Recap puts 2026 commercial investment at €2bn to September (+7% YoY) and the third quarter at €630M (+33%). International investors drove 75% of the quarter; core and core-plus made up over 80%. "Confirms the confidence in our market's potential," says Dils Portugal CEO Pedro Lancastre.
items.why: A market this dependent on foreign core capital is stable but rate-sensitive — flows track global cost-of-capital more than local sentiment.

items.headline: Lisbon offices tighten to 8.4% availability
items.summary: Lisbon office availability fell to 8.4% (the centre below 5%) and prime CBD rent held at €32/m²/month, even as nine-month office investment of €175M sat about 40% under 2025. A 231,000 m² Lisbon pipeline looms over the next two years.
items.why: This is a two-speed office market — scarcity of good central space, not of capital, is setting rents, which favours refurbishment plays over ground-up.

items.headline: Prime yields compress as buyers crowd in
items.summary: Prime high-street retail yields tightened 25bp to 4.25% after deals in Chiado, where rents now reach €155/m²/month; logistics holds at 5.75% in Lisbon and Porto, and prime hotels at 5.75%.
items.why: Compression on prime is the clearest signal competition is back — entry pricing now rewards underwriting discipline over deal access.

readForFund.text: With prime yields compressing, the edge is pricing discipline, not finding the deal.
Nine-month volume already tops all of 2025 and demand is up 60% — the clearest income story on the board.
Investment is down ~40% but central availability is under 5% — scarcity of quality, not of capital.
Foreign core/core-plus is 80%+ of flow — priced for stability, so value-add must earn its risk premium.

editions.label: 10 Nov
editions.title: Portugal hits €2bn in property deals — foreign money now 75% of Q3
editions.summary: Commercial real-estate investment in Portugal reached about €2bn in the first nine months of 2026, with the third quarter alone at €630m — up 33% on Q2. Foreign investors supplied 75% of that Q3 capital, and more than 80% of deals by value went into standing, income-producing assets. Hotels have already beaten their full-year 2024 and 2025 totals at €590m, and industrial has passed all of 2025 at €384m. CBRE now sees the year closing above €3bn. Beneath the headline numbers the squeeze is real: house prices rose 7.5% in October to a new record, build costs keep climbing, and 7% of rental listings vanish within a day. Net: capital wants in, product is scarce — the edge belongs to those who can build or source, not simply buy.
editions.hook: Portugal's €2bn property year is mostly foreign money.

items.headline: Prowinko sells Wells' Chiado building to a private investor
items.summary: Dutch-origin group Prowinko has offloaded its Rua Garrett asset in Lisbon's Chiado — home to a Wells store — to a private buyer. The price was not disclosed.
items.why: Prime Chiado high-street assets rarely trade; a private buyer stepping up signals continued appetite for trophy Lisbon retail even as institutional money chases scale elsewhere.

items.headline: Forum Algarve and Tróia Design Hotel change hands as new names enter
items.summary: Among 2026's marquee trades, Forum Algarve in Faro was sold — marking Alfana Investment Management's entry into Portugal — while Arrow Global acquired the Tróia Design Hotel.
items.why: New institutional entrants and platform buyers taking landmark retail and resort assets show Portugal broadening beyond its usual investor base — a deeper buyer pool supports exit pricing.

items.headline: A €40M Azores Retail Park opens 27 November
items.summary: A new €40M retail park with 11 shops and a pharmacy opens on 27 November, with promoters projecting 550 direct and indirect jobs.
items.why: Retail-park development is back as a yield play; islands and secondary cities offer land and footfall that crowded mainland metros no longer do.

items.headline: JPS Group launches phase 2 of Herdade Real de Santiago on a 10/90 plan
items.summary: The second phase of Herdade Real de Santiago in Pegões is now selling, with apartments from €264,500 and a payment plan of 10% on signing and 90% at the deed.
items.why: Buyer-friendly 10/90 structures are spreading as developers work to hold sales velocity against stretched affordability — a tactic worth tracking for pricing power.

items.headline: Galp's Lisbon headquarters earns WELL Platinum
items.summary: Galp's Lisbon HQ has achieved WELL Platinum certification, among the highest marks for buildings designed around occupant health and wellbeing.
items.why: Wellness and green ratings increasingly command rent premiums and are becoming table stakes for prime corporate tenants — a design decision with a direct yield effect.

items.headline: Concreta 2026 reframes the future of architecture and construction
items.summary: Concreta, Portugal's main architecture and construction fair, returns with a programme centred on where building design, materials and methods are heading next.
items.why: The sector's innovation agenda — industrialised construction, retrofit, sustainability — directly shapes the build costs and timelines that drive development returns.

items.headline: Portugal draws ~€2bn in commercial investment over nine months
items.summary: Commercial volume hit roughly €2bn in Jan–Sep (per Dils), with Q3 at €630m, up 33% q/q and foreign buyers at 75%. Retail led Q3 at €195m, hotels have topped their 2024 and 2025 full-year totals, and industrial has already beaten all of 2025; CBRE sees the year above €3bn.
items.why: Momentum and a widening foreign-capital base support values, but with 80%+ of volume in standing assets, the scarcity is development-grade product — the gap build-and-source strategies fill.

items.headline: House prices climb 7.5% in October to a new record
items.summary: Portuguese house prices rose 7.5% year on year in October, hitting a fresh all-time high, according to idealista's index.
items.why: Persistent price growth confirms structural undersupply, underpinning land and residential development economics — while tightening affordability and exit-buyer depth.

items.headline: Building costs keep rising, squeezing new-build margins
items.summary: The cost of building new homes in Portugal continues its steady climb, idealista reports, extending a multi-year run of construction-cost inflation.
items.why: Rising hard costs compress developer margins and lift the price floor for viable schemes — underwriting must assume cost escalation, not hold it constant.

readForFund.lead: Underwrite the gap, not the average.
readForFund.text: With 80%+ of capital chasing standing assets, development-grade product is the scarce commodity — origination beats auction.

readForFund.lead: Foreign capital is the marginal buyer.
readForFund.text: At 75% of Q3, overseas money is setting pricing — align product and reporting to institutional, cross-border expectations.

readForFund.lead: Margin lives in the cost line.
readForFund.text: Prices at records but build costs still rising means returns come from procurement and delivery, not from resale assumptions.
10/90 payment plans and wellness-certified product are how sellers hold velocity and rent as buyers stretch.

editions.label: 9 Nov
editions.title: €2bn into Portuguese property in nine months — Q3 up 33%, foreign buyers now 75%
editions.summary: Portugal pulled in roughly €2bn of commercial property investment in the first nine months of 2026, and the pace is quickening rather than cooling. Third-quarter volume hit €630m — up 33% on the prior quarter, per Dils. Foreign capital drove 75% of it, and more than 80% went into core and core-plus assets — buyers want income, not risk. Hotels have already beaten their full-year totals for both 2024 and 2025, with €590m banked. Retail led the quarter on the Forum Algarve sale; logistics is already above all of last year. CBRE sees the full year topping €3bn. Net: the money is here, it's foreign, and it's chasing stabilised cash flow.
editions.hook: Capital isn't slowing: €2bn placed by September, and the quarter accelerated.

items.headline: Alfana enters Portugal with Forum Algarve
items.summary: London-based Alfana Investment Management bought the Faro shopping centre for its new Rivoli Retail platform — its first deal in Portugal. Retail was Q3's most active segment at €195m (31% of the quarter), and prime Chiado high-street yields compressed 25bps to 4.25%.
items.why: A fresh institutional entrant and yield compression on the best high street say retail — written off a few years ago — is back in favour with cross-border capital.

items.headline: Arrow Global buys the Tróia Design Hotel
items.summary: The Setúbal resort hotel changed hands in the quarter's largest hospitality deal. Hotels have drawn €590m so far this year — more than the full-year totals of either 2024 or 2025 — and now make up 27% of all commercial investment, with prime yields near 5.75%.
items.why: Record tourism — 83m overnight stays in the year to August — keeps hospitality the single hottest asset class; expect more platform plays and portfolio trades.

items.headline: Saqax takes Logispark Montijo from CBRE IM
items.summary: Dutch investor Saqax acquired the Montijo logistics park from CBRE Investment Management, and a data-centre purchase in Évora also closed. Industrial & logistics investment of €384m year-to-date already tops all of 2025, with prime yields at 5.75%.
items.why: Industrial take-up jumped 60% while licensing delays throttle new supply — the classic undersupplied-demand setup that underpins rents and values.

items.headline: Licences filed for 61,000+ homes — but keys are years away
items.summary: Municipalities received licensing requests for 61,334 homes across ~18,000 projects in the first nine months, per Confidencial Imobiliário — a monthly pace 12% above 2025. The Lisbon and Porto metros absorb 41%; Porto city leads the country with 4,174 homes.
items.why: The pipeline is finally filling, but the four-year-plus path from licence to handover means today's record prices won't be eased by new supply this decade.

items.headline: Asking prices rise 7.5% in October to a new record
items.summary: idealista's asking-price index climbed 7.5% year-on-year in October, another all-time high for homes on the market in Portugal. Prices keep setting records even as transaction growth has cooled from its mid-year peak.
items.why: Record prices on slowing volume point to a supply-constrained market — supportive of values, but a widening affordability gap that keeps regulatory risk on the table.

items.headline: CBRE tips a €3bn+ year as deals queue for Q4
items.summary: With ~€2bn done by September, CBRE forecasts full-year commercial investment above €3bn on deals expected to close in Q4; Worx pencils in €2.6–2.75bn. The estimates diverge by methodology, but all point up.
items.why: A strong Q4 close would confirm a clear recovery from the rate-driven lull — and set a competitive pricing backdrop for anyone underwriting Portuguese assets into 2027.

items.headline: Where the rental-law overhaul stands: faster evictions, looser caps
items.summary: The government's arrendamento reform passed in principle and is now in committee under a PSD–Chega deal. Core changes: eviction proceedings after two months of arrears (down from three), removal of the 2% cap on new-contract rents, up to three deposits, elderly-tenant protections and tax relief for landlords who let. Ministers aim to pass it by year-end.
items.why: If enacted, the package tilts the rental market toward landlords and funds — faster recourse, freer pricing — and could draw more stock into the formal rental market that income investors target.

readForFund.text: With 80%+ of capital in core/core-plus and foreign buyers at 75%, the edge is pricing stabilised income sharper than the next cross-border bidder — not sourcing.

readForFund.lead: Hotels and logistics are where the heat is.
readForFund.text: Both have already beaten 2025's full-year volume; yields near 5.75% and structural undersupply make them the clearest risk-adjusted entries right now.
A looser rent cap and faster evictions, if passed by year-end, improve the arithmetic on residential and build-to-rent — but watch the affordability politics that could reverse it.
61,000 homes in licensing won't hit the market before the end of the decade, so the price-support thesis holds through this fund's acquisition window.
